newsitem.title: GERMANY: No wanted Nazis on Swiss bank list - German centre.
newsitem.headline: No wanted Nazis on Swiss bank list - German centre.

text.p: Germany's centre for the investigation of Nazi crimes has found no trace of anyone still wanted for wartime atrocities on the list of dormant Holocaust-era accounts published by Swiss banks.

Willi Dressen, the head of the Ludwigsburg-based centre, said on Friday his staff had checked the 2,000 names on the list against their own files. "We have not found anyone with the same name as people who are wanted," he said.
The Los Angeles-based Simon Wiesenthal centre said after the banks published their list last month that it may include several members of Adolf Hitler's elite.
Dressen said between 150 and 200 names in the centre's files could match those on the banks' lists but they were not those of wanted people or suspects.

The centre holds more than one million files, including those on former members of the Wehrmacht, Germany's wartime army, and the notorious SS elite fighting force. But it also contains records of victims of Nazi persecution and witnesses.

Dressen said that, while some names matched, this was no guarantee that people on the list were the same as those on his files. Many of the names were very common and the Swiss banks had not provided the dates of birth of the account holders, he said.
